newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Group of Serbian protesters stones police.
newsitem.headline: Group of Serbian protesters stones police.

text.p: About 200 militant demonstrators hurled stones, bottles and pieces of cement at Serbian police in Belgrade on Monday after a main body of protesters dispersed peacefully to end a standoff with security forces.

A Reuters news team on the scene said police were initially restrained, doing nothing more than raising their shields to deflect projectiles. But after being repeatedly challenged they started chasing the protesters.

It was the second straight day of clashes between opposition protesters and the feared security police of autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic in a largely peaceful three-month period of street protests against alleged election fraud.

Most of several hundred police wearing helmets and body armour had withdrawn after tens of thousands of demonstrators withdrew from a standoff with a police cordon on a major boulevard earlier in the afternoon.
But about 200 extremists lingered for what may have been the first unprovoked assault by protesters on police in Serbia's marathon political crisis.

Police finally charged, pursuing scattered clutches of protesters in different directions past startled strollers in the downtown shopping district. Several protesters were caught, kicked and clubbed by police.
